newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - NAB down in Australia, strong overseas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - NAB down in Australia, strong overseas.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd's Australian operations reported a slightly lower profit in the year to September 30 but operations in the United States, New Zealand and Britain made strong profit contributions.
Profit after tax from NAB's Australian operations fell to A$1.277 billion for the year to September 30 from A$1.284 billion a year earlier.
"Underlying profit grew by 4.1 percent, but was offset by a rise in the charge for bad and doubtful debts from A$78 million to A$185 million," NAB managing director Don Argus said.
The Australian result represented a creditable performance in difficult conditions, Argus said in a statement accompanying the results.
"Competition in Australia was stronger than in any other market in which the group operated during the year," he said, adding that NAB's domestic interest margin fell to 3.7 percent from 4.3 percent.

NAB said net interest income from Australia grew in line with expectations to A$2.59 billion from A$2.49 billion, while other operating income including fees and charges rose to A$1.58 billion from A$1.47 billion.

"Credit card income continued to grow with the Fly Buys loyalty programme a major factor with outstandings increasing by 18 percent," NAB said, adding leasing income showed a strong rise in Australia.
"The significant increase in the charge for doubtful debts from the very low prior year level reflected the subdued activity levels in the economy," it said.

The profit contribution from NAB's operations in Britain and Ireland fell to A$403 million from A$420 million a year earlier, due in large part to the stronger Australian dollar and a higher provision for bad and doubtful debts.

NAB said that profits from the British and Irish operations actually rose 2.6 percent in local currency terms. Profits from the Bank of New Zealand rose 5.7 percent to A$279 million, due to strong growth in net interest and other income.

The biggest surge in profits from overseas came from the Michigan National Corp in the United States, which was acquired in November last year and produced a net profit of A$158 million. Comparisons were not available.
"Michigan has performed consistently through the year with the 11 month results being in line with our expectations," NAB said.
Earlier NAB reported a 6.8 percent rise in group net profit A$2.10 billion for the year, above the average analyst expectation of about A$2.01 billion.
NAB shares were up 20 cents at A$14.12 at 1.00 p.m. (0200 GMT).
